title: Active-standby readiness protocol for regional routing and model-fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a deterministic readiness protocol and orchestration steps to ensure warm-standby regions and fallback model variants are verified and promotable with minimal latency/regression risk when primary regions degrade. Scope includes: health probe design, KV-cache priming checks, model-variant compatibility verification, tier-aware traffic fencing, and an automated 'promote-on-pass' flow that ties into Smart Routing policies. Out of scope: changes to pricing tiers and long-term autoscaler algorithms (separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Warm-standby region can be validated within 90s using non-customer traffic probes without affecting SLOs.
A2: KV-cache priming check verifies model variant keyspace compatibility and reports warm percentage >= 70% before promotion.
A3: Orchestration runbook can perform a dry-run failover that routes 0.1% test traffic to standby and confirms end-to-end request/response parity within 5% latency increase.
A4: Automated fallback picks model variant from configured policy and rolls back to previous model if quality regressions exceed threshold in evals pipeline.
A5: New metrics (standby_readiness_score, kv_warm_pct, last_probe_status) are visible in Console per-customer and per-region.
A6: Playbook documented and verified by SRE and PD; security review completed for probes and data handling.
implementation_notes: Design probes as staged checks: control-plane reachability -> runtime light inference -> KV cache warmness -> model-variant tokenization sanity.
Use isolated 'probe' API key space so probes don't inflate customer billing; probe requests are tagged and filtered in analytics.
Introduce a readiness state machine: UNKNOWN -> PROBING -> READY -> DEGRADED -> PROMOTE_BLOCKED. State persisted in cluster metadata with TTLs.
KV warmness heuristic: sample top-10 most-recent prefixes for the customer's request mix; compute percent of cache hits on 100 probe tokens.
Fallback selection: prefer same-architecture quantized variant (e.g., fp16 -> 4-bit) with precomputed compatibility matrix to avoid runtime failures.
Operational knobs: max_probe_rps per region, probe_backoff_exponent for repeated failures, and manual override via Console.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gated merge to main with default OFF; unit and integration tests in CI.
2) Internal dogfood: enable for infra-only tenants in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for 72h; run automated dry-run failovers daily.
3) Gradual opt-in: expose to limited customers behind a console toggle and collect readiness metrics for two weeks.
4) Full enablement for region-level routing policies after 2 successful customer trials and SRE sign-off.
5) Post-rollout: run synthetic chaos scenarios quarterly to validate protocol resilience.
testing_plan: Unit tests covering state transitions and TTL expiry.
Integration tests against a local runtime shim that simulates KV cache hit/miss and model-variant loading delays.
End-to-end canary: route 0.1% of real traffic through promote flow; compare semantic similarity using rearranged eval suite.
Load test: confirm probes at max_probe_rps do not increase p95 latency by more than 2ms in host region.
Regression test: automated eval checks disallow promotion if selected fallback increases hallucination rate by >3% on customer prompt set.
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards: Standby Readiness Overview (global), Per-Customer Region Readiness, Probe Failure Trends.
Alerts: standby_readiness_score < 0.5 for >5m triggers SRE paging (P1).
SLO guardrails: block auto-promotion if recent rollback > 1 in last 24h for same customer.
Audit logs: keep probe request/response hashes (redacted) for 30 days; surface in Console for incident debugging.
Cost telemetry: estimate additional RPS and GPU seconds due to priming probes; cap by tier.
